result:
I've written the design for experiment 28 to `runs/pending_experiment.json`, and the JSON parses. Nothing has been trained yet.

**What it changes:** the camera frame is enlarged inside the model to 288 px before the two EfficientNet-B0 trunks, up from 224 px. That one constant (`INPUT_PX` in `model/model.py`) is the whole change. The two feature maps the model reads grow from 14×14 and 7×7 to 18×18 and 9×9. There are no new parameters, so the exported file stays at about 31.7 MB. The training recipe is unchanged: 8 epochs, weight averaging from epoch 5, the same augmentation and the same style mixing.

**Why this lever:**
- Experiment 15 is the only time this era changed the input size (128 → 224 px). With no new parameters, it took usable fixes on the held-out 2024 photograph from 65.5% to 74.25%. Nobody has tried a larger size since.
- On this ruler, the big gains on the never-seen photograph have all come from the pretrained trunk. Every attempt since the champion to build survey-robustness through training has come back worse than 0.0777 (consistency loss, continuous vantages, patchwork, probe-then-fine-tune, Noisy Student weights).
- A bigger trunk would break the size limit (31.7 of 33.6 MB used). A larger input lets the existing trunk see more of the small, stable structure (streets, building footprints, kerbs) without adding weight.

**Expected result:** mission score from 0.0777 to roughly 0.055–0.065. That means usable fixes rising from 93.0% to about 94.5–95%, mostly by abstaining on fewer frames, with false fixes staying at or below 1%. Host latency should go from about 49 ms to about 80 ms, well under the 250 ms limit. Training should take about 1.6× longer (around 3 h instead of 1.8 h).

**Measurement noise:** the eval has 400 frames, so a gap of about ±0.005 is only two frames. If usable stays flat within that band, the result says enlarging further than 224 px stopped helping.

The implementation brief says to keep batch size 64 and not to shrink it if memory runs out, because that would make it a second change. It restates the ONNX input/output and CLI contracts, and the rule that nothing under `model/` may open the 2024 photograph.
